problems.title: Missing colon
problems.promptMd: This program should print `ok` if the input number is positive and `no` otherwise. It does not run. Fix the syntax error and leave the behavior the same.
problems.starterCode:
n = int(input())
if n > 0
    print("ok")
else:
    print("no")
problems.explanationMd: The `if` header is missing its trailing colon.

problems.title: Find the logical error
problems.promptMd: The program should print the sum of the integers from 1 through n, where n is the input. It compiles and runs, but the result is wrong. Which statement best describes the bug?
problems.starterCode:
n = int(input())
s = 0
for i in range(1, n):
    s += i
print(s)
problems.explanationMd: `range(1, n)` stops before n, so the last term is missing. The stop value must be `n + 1`.

options.text: The loop includes n one time too many.
The loop never adds n, because range stops before n.
int(input()) cannot read a positive integer.

problems.title: Sum the numbers
problems.promptMd: The first line of input is an integer n. The second line contains n integers. Print their sum. The starter returns 0 for every input. Fix it.
problems.starterCode:
n = int(input())
nums = list(map(int, input().split()))
print(0)
problems.explanationMd: Print the sum of `nums` instead of 0.
